caption: The five parenthesizations of four group-type defect lines form a directed pentagon. Three associator steps from (((gh)k)l) to g(h(kl)) carry omega(g,h,k) omega(g,hk,l) omega(h,k,l); the two-step route carries omega(gh,k,l) omega(g,h,kl).

The two three-line fusion trees have rephasing factors u(g,h) and u(gh,k) on the left junctions, and u(h,k) and u(g,hk) on the right junctions. With each pair junction m-prime equal to u times m and F(alpha) equal to omega, omega prime equals omega times the product of right factors divided by the product of left factors.

Three restricted sitewise symmetry operators act on the same spatial region R. The highlighted column is one site j; the vertical guides mark the same sites in all three rows. Multiplying g and h first or h and k first gives the same operator U_ghk(R), providing a coherent junction choice with trivial three-cocycle class. The drawn number and spacing of sites are schematic.
At one time, the spatial symmetry cut C_g meets the boundary of Sigma at x_L and x_R, the endpoints of interval I.
Continuing the same cut C_g over I_t gives a two-dimensional sheet S_g. It meets the boundary spacetime along two vertical edges.
The isolated boundary spacetime contains exactly the two endpoint worldlines, {x_L,x_R} × I_t.

Four separate physical sites each contain four group-valued components. One highlighted component from each site enters the central plaquette state, where all four share a group value z and are summed over z. The open dots belong to other neighboring plaquettes.

One physical bulk site has four group-valued components. Its onsite g action multiplies all four labels by g and carries four oriented cocycle edge factors: two direct factors and two inverse factors.

At an open boundary, linked components across adjacent physical sites share one group value alpha_i. The neighboring linked cluster has independent value alpha_i+1. The oriented lower edge of the central physical site is the boundary bond with input labels (alpha_i, alpha_i+1).

The product onsite symmetry acts on an open six-site bulk patch. Interior labels are reindexed within their group sums, while inverse phase factors on matched internal edges cancel. On each rightward physical boundary bond a factor f_g=q_g inverse remains, evaluated on the input edge labels; the output edge labels are g alpha.

The effective edge symmetry maps each boundary group label alpha_i to g alpha_i while also multiplying the state by a cocycle-dependent phase on each adjacent pair. Orange capsules on the input bonds show where the pair phases act; violet vertical arrows show the site-label transformation. The displayed fixed-point-basis formula summarizes these two simultaneous factors.

On the boundary x–t worldsheet, the full edge symmetry inserted at one time occupies a whole spatial slice. Restricting it to interval I retains only its internal bonds and omits bonds crossing the endpoints. The shaded region marks where g acts; continuing the two endpoints over I_t gives their two worldlines.

For two adjacent boundary bonds the relative phases are lambda(a)/lambda(b) and lambda(b)/lambda(c), so the middle factor cancels and only endpoint factors remain. At endpoint a a local reduction junction for g and h carries the inverse phase, in the displayed convention.

At one boundary endpoint the two orders of reducing three symmetry actions leave two lambda factors each before their inverse reduction maps act. The left residual product uses lambda_g,h(k a) and lambda_gh,k(a); the right uses lambda_h,k(a) and lambda_g,hk(a). The quotient of residual products equals the right-to-left quotient of the inverse junction maps, defining the boundary associator in the adopted convention.

The left tetrahedron has successive vertex labels 1,g,gh,ghk and ordered edges g,h,k. On the right, the same ordered labels enter two boundary symmetry-tensor reduction trees. Their associator carries an edge phase; for the corresponding group-cohomology SPT the bulk and edge H3 classes agree.

The left panel draws the action of one symmetry line a on an input vacuum m_i as a direct sum of output sectors; branch labels n^a_ji and n^a_ki count independent junction channels. The right panel keeps one vacuum m on both sides while n^a_11 still counts a space of junction channels. The ellipsis denotes arbitrary further channels.

Start with the full fusion category C, including symmetry lines, fusion, and junctions. A fiber functor C to Vec is the rank-one test: if one exists, it gives a single-vacuum symmetric gapped phase, and inequivalent functors distinguish SPT phases. Without one, a unique symmetric gap is obstructed while multiple-vacuum or gapless phases remain possible. A fixed microscopic symmetry action, local charges, and interfaces provide a further realization and diagnostic question.
